title: Cross-team cadence: Q3 Dedicated Capacity Trajectory & Autoscale Playbook (pilot metrics + rollback criteria)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: produce an operational playbook and quarter-long trajectory for Dedicated capacity autoscaling that teams can adopt with clear pilot metrics, governance checkpoints, and fast rollback criteria. This ticket coordinates PM/Eng/Infra/Console to: (1) define success metrics for a Q3 pilot, (2) design governance gates for capacity hedging and burst policies, (3) publish a step-by-step canary/rollback checklist and cost guardrails, and (4) instrument dashboards and alerts needed to run the pilot safely. The focus is production readiness rather than exploratory experiments: defaults, owner responsibilities, and SLO-aligned thresholds must be explicit.
acceptance_criteria: Pilot runbook published in Confluence with roles and run cadence
Canary criteria defined: p95 latency < 120ms, error rate < 0.5%, token cost variance < 7%
Rollback triggers documented and automated where possible (dashboard + PagerDuty playbook)
End-to-end telemetry (throughput, cold-start fraction, cache hit rate) visible on dedicated-capacity Grafana panel
One pilot region (us-west) completes a 2-week smoketest with no customer-impact incidents and sign-off from runtime SRE, PM, and Console owners
milestones: 2026-03-01: Draft runbook + Canary thresholds submitted for review
2026-03-22: Instrumentation PR merged (ENG-3221) and Grafana panels live
2026-04-19: Pilot review, metrics validation, and decision: scale/iterate/rollback
2026-05-10: Formalize governance playbook and publish to org
risks: Undetected regression in tail latency when autoscale intersects with KV cache eviction
Cost leakage during sustained bursts if hedging policy is too permissive
Cross-team misalignment on SLO ownership (runtime vs customer-facing teams)
Insufficient telemetry to automate rollback leading to slower manual intervention
notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive pre-warming reduces cold-start but increases baseline cost; conservative hedging reduces spend but increases risk of throttling during spike.
We will use a layered policy: soft hedges (predictive warm pools) + hard caps (emergency throttle) + graceful degradation paths (lower-cost model variants).
Aim to keep cost delta for pilot < 10% relative to baseline while improving P95 for burst traffic by 20%.
